text.p: Belgian police are investigating match fixing allegations surrounding the 1984 UEFA Cup semifinal between Anderlecht and England's Nottingham Forest, Belgian media said on Wednesday.

The probe was launched after the Belgian club told police it was being blackmailed by a man who claimed to have acted as an intermediary to fix the second leg match, which the Belgian side won 3-0 after losing the first leg 2-0.
The result took Anderlecht to the final, which they lost to another English club, Tottenham Hotspur.

Anderlecht's current manager Michel Verschueren confirmed police had been asked to investigate the alleged blackmail attempt. But he denied the central allegation that the club used an intermediary to try to "buy" the game.
"No. Absolutely not," Verschueren told RTL-TVI television.
There is no suggestion made in the allegations that Nottingham Forest or its players were involved.
BRTN said a former official of the club had paid about 20 million francs ($572,000) to a blackmailer, who claimed to have a taped recording backing up his match fixing claims.
Verschueren said a blackmail attempt had been successful but declined to say how much had been paid.
"(The official) was frightened about the image of the club suffering (from the tape) and was blackmailed. It's true," he told RTL-TVI.
He said however the tape was a forgery, made up of an amalgam of recordings, edited to give a false impression about a conversation said to have taken place about the 1984 game.
Police were called in after a further blackmail attempt was made, Verschueren added.
BRTN said the public prosecutor's office was investigating two men for blackmail. A spokesman for the prosecutor's office was not immediately available to comment.
The Belgian soccer union had been informed but had not looked into the case and instead passed on the information to UEFA, where a spokeswoman said the case was under investigation, BRTN said.
